Gustavo Ramirez, who helps run the restaurant and is the son of North Beach Pizza Berkeley’s owner of the same name, confirmed to Nosh that the pizza spot will be relocating to 2072 University Avenue, which formerly housed Bobby G’s Pizzeria. The San Francisco pizza chain was first opened in the North Beach neighborhood in 1982 by Brazilian native and Bay Area businessman Altamir Souza, whose price-friendly menu and early adoption of a digital delivery system appealed to San Franciscans looking for a quick bite. Four years later, Souza opened his second location a block away, before moving on to open three others across the city. Souza later expanded across the Bay to San Mateo, Daly City, Half Moon Bay and Berkeley. Over the last few decades, the restaurant chain has switched ownership across its locations. Now, Ramirez’s family owns seven of the remaining restaurants, while Souza owns the remaining one in San Francisco’s Outer Sunset neighborhood. According to Ramirez, this isn’t just a relocation — it’s a homecoming. “So years ago we were actually located on University Avenue at 1598 University Ave. and North Beach Pizza was there for many years,” Ramirez explained. “But then the land was sold to developers so we had to move and we relocated to where we are now, 2420 Shattuck Ave.” Bobby G’s abruptly closed in April, following a lawsuit from a former employee and, as Nosh reported, a pattern of delayed payments and other managerial issues. Once the former Bobby G’s space became available, Ramirez and his family jumped at the chance to sign a lease. “It was just really ideal, really perfect. Everything kind of lined up perfectly for us to be able to make that move back to University Avenue,” Ramirez said. “We signed a lease this month in Berkeley, and we’ve been fixing things up and getting the store ready. And if all goes well, we expect to open within the next few weeks.” Ramirez also confirmed that the restaurant’s menu won’t change, and patrons can expect classics like the pepperoni pizza, cheese stromboli, and crispy chicken parmigiana, alongside its more unique offerings, like the Alcatraz pizza, a ranch sauced pizza pie topped with chicken, gorgonzola, red onions and a spiral of Buffalo sauce. title: Goldman Q3 Earnings Beat on Strong Equities & IB Revenues, Shares Rise - TradingView
content: The Goldman Sachs Group, Inc. GS has reported third-quarter 2026 earnings per share of $17.01, which topped the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 31.9%. The metric also jumped 39% from $12.25 a year ago. Driven by robust client activity, Goldman posted net revenues of $6.44 billion in Equities, which jumped 72% year over year, while fixed income, currencies and commodities (FICC) revenues remained essentially unchanged at $3.47 billion. Strong dealmaking activity lifted investment banking (IB) fees 21% to $3.22 billion, supported by higher advisory, equity underwriting and debt underwriting revenues. Driven by these positives, shares of Goldman rose nearly 3% in the early trading session. A full day’s trading session will depict a clearer picture. Goldman’s overall results benefited from strong revenue growth in the Global Banking & Markets and Asset & Wealth Management businesses, while profitability was highlighted by an annualized return on equity of 18.7%. However, higher operating expenses and increased provisions for credit losses created headwinds. Net earnings attributable to common shareholders were $5.12 billion, up 33% year over year. Net revenues were $18.68 billion, rising 23% year over year and comfortably surpassing the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $16.87 billion by 10.75%. Total non-interest revenues were $14.91 billion, up 32% year over year. The increase reflected higher investment banking revenues, investment management revenues, commissions and fees, and market-making revenues, partially offset by lower other principal transactions revenues. Net interest income was $3.77 billion, down 2% from the prior-year quarter. On the cost side, operating expenses were $11.31 billion, up 20% from the prior-year quarter. Management attributed the increase primarily to significantly higher transaction-based expenses and higher compensation and benefits expenses, reflecting improved operating performance. Even with higher costs, Goldman’s efficiency ratio declined 180 basis points to 60.5% for the quarter. Provision for credit losses was $368 million, up from $339 million in the year-ago quarter, primarily reflecting impairments related to wholesale loans. The Asset & Wealth Management business generated net revenues of $5.05 billion, up 14% year over year. The increase primarily reflected significantly higher management and other fees, driven by higher average assets under supervision, and higher incentive fees from fund distributions. These positives were partially offset by lower investments and private banking, and lending revenues. Total assets under supervision increased to a record $4.10 trillion, reflecting $83 billion in total net inflows and $97 billion in long-term net inflows during the quarter. The Global Banking & Markets business generated net revenues of $13.46 billion, up 32% year over year. Growth was driven by significantly higher Equities revenues and increased investment banking fees, while FICC revenues remained essentially unchanged. Equities benefited from significantly higher financing and intermediation revenues, while investment banking fees were supported by higher advisory, equity underwriting and debt underwriting revenues. The Platform Solutions business reported net revenues of $170 million, down 72% from the year-ago quarter. The decline primarily reflected net markdowns related to the Apple Card loan portfolio, which had previously been transferred to held for sale. Goldman ended the third quarter with total assets of $2.18 trillion, up from $2.13 trillion at the end of the second quarter, while deposits were $568 billion compared with $558 billion in the previous quarter. Total loans increased sequentially to $276 billion from $261 billion. Capital ratios showed mixed trends sequentially. The standardized CET1 capital ratio declined to 12.4% from 12.9%, while the advanced CET1 ratio remained unchanged at 13.6%. The supplementary leverage ratio was stable at 4.3%. During the quarter, Goldman returned $4.49 billion to shareholders, including $3 billion in common share repurchases and $1.49 billion in common stock dividends. Moreover, the company declared a quarterly dividend of $5 per share, payable Dec. 30, 2026. Goldman delivered strong third-quarter results, fueled by robust Equities performance and higher IB revenues. Solid client activity, strong capital markets execution and continued momentum in Asset & Wealth Management drove the results. The IG Wealth Management collaboration, and planned LCN and NEOS acquisitions are likely to strengthen Asset & Wealth Management. While higher operating expenses and increased credit costs remain worth monitoring, record assets under supervision, growth in loans and deposits and continued capital distributions highlight the company’s operating performance. title: CVS Ferrari expands German dealer network with GS-Gabelstapler service - American Journal of Transportation
content:
AJOT Newsroom
	

		 | Oct 13 2026 at 09:44 AM  | Logistics CVS Ferrari is expanding its sales and customer support network in Germany through a new partnership with GS- Gabelstapler Service GmbH. GS-Gabelstapler Service GmbH is the first independent dealer appointed by CVS Ferrari Deutschland in the German-speaking market of Germany, Austria and Switzerland. CVS Ferrari plans to add more regional partners over time. GS-Gabelstapler Service supports the movement, storage, and handling of materials within warehouses, terminals, and industrial facilities. Its services include new and used forklift sales, parts, maintenance, rentals, operator training, and equipment financing, including leasing and installment-purchase options. GS will also add CVS heavy-duty lift trucks to its rental and demonstration fleet. CVS Director, Robert Taylor, said, “CVS is so proud to bring GS Gabelstapler into our growing family in Europe. It is an honor for such an astute material handling company to be representing our product. We look for a great future together, serving our customers.” Kai-Norman Knötsch, Managing Director of CVS Ferrari Deutschland, commented, “Our customers expect advice and service to be available as close to them as possible. With GS, we have found a partner who knows its region and its requirements extremely well. For us, this marks the beginning of a network that we intend to expand step by step in order to provide even better support to our customers.” Torsten Franke, Managing Director of GS-Gabelstapler Service, remarked, “We have known our customers’ requirements for decades and know where heavy-duty equipment is needed. With CVS, we are expanding our product range and closing a gap in our portfolio. Objective, partnership-based advice, comprehensive solutions and service have been the hallmarks of our company for more than 45 years. We are now delighted to be able to offer our customers CVS products for heavy-duty handling and container loading as well.” CVS Ferrari Deutschland supplies equipment for ports, terminals, industrial operations and other demanding material-handling applications. The product line includes reach stackers for loaded and empty containers, mast-style empty container handlers for depots and port facilities, high-capacity lift trucks, and terminal tractors available in two-wheel-drive and four-wheel-drive configurations. CVS reach stackers can stack containers up to six high. Certain mast-style empty container handlers can stack up to eight containers high and, depending on configuration, handle two empty containers at the same time. Heavy-duty lift trucks are available with rated capacities from 16 to 52 metric tons, approximately 35,300 to 114,600 pounds. Electric-drive empty container handlers and terminal tractors are also available to help customers address emissions and noise requirements at ports and terminals. “High-quality products, sound advice, and first-class service are what distinguish us. With GS, we now have a partner at our side who enables us to fully meet these requirements. For us, this marks the beginning of a network that we intend to expand step by step in order to provide even better support to our customers,” said Oliver Hoffmann, Sales Manager, CVS Ferrari Deutschland. Good morning. My name is [Katie] and I will be your conference facilitator today. I would like to welcome everyone to The Goldman Sachs third quarter 2026 earnings conference call. On behalf of Goldman Sachs, I will begin the call with the following disclaimer. The earnings presentation can be found on the investor relations page of the goldmansachs.com website and contains information on forward-looking statements and non-GAAP measures. This audiocast is copyrighted material of The Goldman Sachs Group Inc., and may not be duplicated, reproduced, or rebroadcast without consent. This call is being recorded today, October 13, 2026. I will now turn the call over to Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, David Solomon, and Chief Financial Officer, Denis Coleman. Thank you. Mr. Solomon, you may begin your conference. Thank you, operator. Good morning, everybody. Thank you for joining us. We delivered very strong performance in the third quarter, generating net revenues of $18.7 billion, the second highest in our history, earnings per share of $17.01, an ROE of 18.7%, and an ROTE of 20.5%. Our quarterly results included the impact of an accelerated charitable contribution. Excluding that contribution, quarterly EPS would've been approximately $18, and ROE and ROTE would've been approximately 20% and 21.5% respectively. For the year-to-date, we delivered record revenues driving an ROE of 20.7% and an ROTE of 22.4%. While the third quarter began with optimism around a potential resolution of the conflict in the Middle East, renewed geopolitical tensions and continued disruption of energy flows added complexity to the outlook, increasing oil prices, reigniting inflation concerns, and driving bond yields higher. Against this backdrop, the Fed raised rates in September for the first time in three years, with markets pricing in approximately 75 basis points of additional tightening in this cycle across the U.S., U.K., and Europe. Despite these crosscurrents, the health of the underlying U.S. economy has remained solid, with strong corporate earnings growth, GDP growth of 2.2%, and a very resilient labor market. In complex environments such as these, clients rely on the advice, execution, and intermediation expertise of Goldman Sachs to navigate uncertainty and advance their most important strategic priorities. In global banking and markets, we generated the second highest revenues in our history. Within investment banking, advisory revenues were a record, and we maintained our longstanding number one position in M&A, advising on $1.5 trillion of announced transactions for the year. We maintained our year-to-date lead over our closest peer of approximately $430 billion, the largest lead we've ever had, as clients turn to us for advice on significant transactions, including Hugging Face's $13 billion sale to NVIDIA and Integer Holdings' $6 billion sale to KKR. As you'll remember, we entered the quarter with our highest backlog in five years, and even with exceptionally strong revenue production in the quarter, our backlog remains very robust, reflecting the strength and breadth of client engagement across our leading investment banking franchise. In equities, we delivered our second-best performance after last quarter's record results, with strength across both intermediation and financing. In FICC, we remain steadfast in supporting our clients' global risk intermediation needs across asset classes amid sharp moves in rates and increased volatility in commodities. Importantly, financing activities have become a larger and more durable component of our markets businesses, representing over 40% of FICC and equities revenues year-to-date. This progress reflects strong client demand, prudent balance sheet deployment, and continued execution against our strategic priorities, including deliberate multi-year investments in Asia, which we highlighted earlier this year as an opportunity to drive further share gains. This dynamic market backdrop has also reinforced the importance of trusted advice and diversified investment solutions for asset and wealth management clients. Our scaled and durable platform brings together leading investment capabilities across public and private markets and delivers them through deep institutional relationships, our ultra-premier high net worth wealth management franchise, and our expanding third-party distribution network. The strength of this platform continues to drive exceptional growth at scale. In the third quarter, management and other fees increased 22% year-over-year to a record $3.6 billion and surpassed $10 billion for the year-to-date. Our assets under supervision reached another record of $4.1 trillion, supported by $97 billion of long-term net inflows, representing our 35th consecutive quarter of inflows. In wealth management, $47 billion of long-term net inflows contributed to record client assets of $2.1 trillion. For 2026, wealth management long-term net inflows are annualizing at 12%, well ahead of our 5% target, which underscores the strength of our client relationships built on trust and long-term performance. In alternatives, we are driving strong growth, with alternative assets under supervision up 26% year-over-year to a record $491 billion. We continue to see strong momentum in fundraising, with $37 billion raised in the quarter, driving a total of $122 billion in fundraising for the year-to-date, reflecting investor demand for experienced investment managers. Considering the strength, we now expect full year fundraising of roughly $150 billion. Given the sustained levels of investment performance for clients, our leading asset and wealth management business remains very well positioned for continued growth amid attractive secular tailwinds. At the same time, we are also inorganically accelerating growth and building a stronger platform with a better product offering for clients. In August, we announced agreements to acquire NEOS, a market leader in derivative income ETFs with approximately $35 billion in AUM at quarter end, and LCN Capital Partners, a leading triple net lease investment manager. The NEOS acquisition would bring our global active ETF assets under supervision to over $90 billion, establishing Goldman Sachs among the top eight providers by assets under supervision and top six by revenue. While LCN broadens the range of private real estate investment solutions we can offer. Importantly, these acquisitions also bring talented and entrepreneurial teams to Goldman Sachs. We remain focused on opportunities that enhance distribution, deepen investment capabilities, and add products to strengthen asset and wealth management. Our bar for strategic financial and cultural fit remains very high, and we will continue to allocate capital dynamically and with discipline as we drive growth. All in, our record year-to-date revenues are the result of years of focused execution that have strengthened our market-leading businesses and increased connectivity across the firm as we harnessed the power of One Goldman Sachs. Importantly, we have created a higher revenue base with our more durable revenues having more than doubled since 2020 Investor Day, and now representing approximately 45% of revenues for the year-to-date. The increased durability, coupled with our expense discipline and prudent capital management, enhances the resilience of our earnings and supports higher returns through the cycle, providing Goldman Sachs with an even stronger foundation for growth. Looking forward, though uncertainty persists, corporates and investors recognize that standing still can be a competitive disadvantage. Clients are taking action to modernize operations, secure critical capabilities, and reallocate capital towards their highest return opportunities. All of this is driving demand for M&A, capital formation, financing, risk management, and advice, playing directly to the strength of our franchise. An ongoing theme has been the growth in AI infrastructure investment. Recent studies estimate that the U.S. data center build-out could require north of $10 trillion in investment through 2032, averaging roughly 3.6% of U.S. GDP annually. In our conversations with clients, demand for compute significantly exceeds supply at the moment, creating opportunities to help develop financing structures to meet that capacity shortfall. Our differentiated financing, distribution, and investing capabilities position us to play a meaningful role in the mobilization of capital and supporting client activity. While we are proud of the privileged position we play in the AI investment cycle, no one knows how the demands for capital and compute will evolve as the broader AI ecosystem matures. That will only become clearer as technology and markets continue to develop. This uncertainty reinforces the importance of remaining vigilant around the types of activity we finance and how we manage risk as we support our clients. We are highly selective about the risk we underwrite and the capital we commit, particularly as client financing needs become larger and more complex. Beyond these financial risks, we also recognize the broader concerns around the accelerating pace of AI technology and the unchecked advancement of frontier models. Like other transformative technologies, AI presents significant opportunities, but also significant risks that must be carefully assessed and managed. However, the choice is not between halting progress and moving forward without guardrails. We must enable innovation and also demand responsibility. The experience of the financial services industry has demonstrated the value of rigorous testing, independent review and continuous monitoring, and clear human accountability. These principles, applied in ways that reflect the unique characteristics of AI, can help build the trust and confidence needed to deploy the technology responsibly at scale while companies, developers, and governments work together to establish appropriate safeguards. All in, we continue to see meaningful opportunities ahead of us. We are incredibly well positioned given our relentless focus on serving our clients while remaining vigilant to emerging risks in this dynamic environment. Our culture of teamwork, excellence, and partnership remains a key differentiator that has enabled us to adapt, innovate, and execute through a range of environments. I've never been more confident in our ability to create long-term value for shareholders by making the right investments to grow the firm and generate sustainable earnings growth. With that, I'll turn it over to Denis to walk through our financial results in more detail. Thank you, David. Good morning, everyone. Let's start with our results on page one of the presentation. In the third quarter, we generated net revenues of $18.7 billion, earnings per share of $17.01, which drove a quarterly ROE of 18.7% and ROTE of 20.5%. Turning to segment performance starting on page three. Global banking and markets revenues were $13.5 billion in the third quarter, our second highest quarterly revenues, contributing to a segment ROE of 23.5% for the year-to-date. Moving to page four, advisory revenues of $1.7 billion reached a quarterly record and rose 18% year-over-year, driven by higher volumes. For the year-to-date, we maintained our number one league table position for announced and completed M&A volumes. In equity underwriting, revenues of $666 million rose 43% year-over-year on strong IPO and secondary offerings activity. In debt underwriting, revenues were $904 million, up 15% year-over-year, driven primarily by stronger investment grade activity. year-to-date, we ranked number one in equity underwriting, number two in leveraged loans, and number three in high yield debt underwriting. Even amid very strong accruals in the quarter, our investment banking backlog remains very robust, as strong revenue realizations and advisory were largely offset by solid replenishment and equity underwriting. year-to-date, sponsor share of announced M&A remains below historical averages, presenting further upside when activity picks up. FICC net revenues were essentially unchanged year-over-year. Intermediation revenues declined 7%, as lower results in mortgages, rates, and credit were largely offset by strong performance in currencies and commodities. Financing revenues increased 14% to their second highest level, driven by strength in mortgages and structured financing. Equities net revenues were $6.4 billion, up 72% year-over-year, representing our second-best quarter, driven by strong performance in both intermediation and financing. Equities intermediation revenues rose 52% to their second highest level, driven by strength in derivatives. Equities financing revenues rose 96% to a record driven primarily by elevated average prime balances and strong activity across Asia. Demand for equities financing continues to exceed available industry capacity, supporting attractive pricing and allowing us to remain selective in deploying resources. Following significant multi-year investment, our focus is increasingly on optimizing a diversified global portfolio, guided by our risk management framework, client relationships, and returns. More broadly, we continue to see structural tailwinds for the growth in tradable assets and the increasing financing needs associated with those assets, which have helped to support sustained industry growth and equities financing over time. Year-to-date, total financing revenues of $12.7 billion were a record and represented over 40% of combined FICC and equities revenues. As David mentioned, growth in financing revenues has contributed to greater durability in FICC and equities, and is underpinned by a robust risk framework that includes diversified exposures, limits, concentration management, and comprehensive stress testing. Let's turn to page five. Asset and wealth management revenues were $5.1 billion, up 14% year-over-year. Management and other fees rose 22% year-over-year to a record $3.6 billion, reflecting the impact of higher average assets under supervision. Incentive fees were $587 million. Through our ultra high net worth wealth management franchise, we provided clients early access to a high growth investment opportunity and recognized incentive fees following the company's IPO. Based on our current outlook, we expect incentive fees to remain elevated in the fourth quarter. Private banking and lending revenues were $827 million, up 20% sequentially, driven by higher net interest from consumer deposits. Loan balances were up 6% to $51 billion. Investments revenues were $50 million, given the timing of certain monetizations following a strong second quarter and certain markdowns. Now moving to page six. Total assets under supervision ended the quarter at a record $4.1 trillion, supported by $97 billion of long-term fee-based net inflows, marking our 35th consecutive quarter of long-term fee-based net inflows. Wealth management client assets reached another record of $2.1 trillion, with $47 billion of long-term net inflows. Turning to page seven. Alternative assets under supervision totaled $491 billion at the end of the third quarter, driving $860 million in management and other fees, the best performance since our 2020 Investor Day. Gross third-party alternatives fundraising was $37 billion for the quarter and $122 billion for the year-to-date. On page nine, firm wide net interest income was $3.8 billion. Our total loan portfolio increased 6% from the prior quarter to $276 billion, reflecting broad-based growth across the portfolio. Our provision for credit losses was $368 million. While overall credit quality and portfolio performance have remained strong, our provisions reflected certain impairments across our portfolio as well as overall growth in lending. Turning to expenses on page 10. Total operating expenses were $11.3 billion for the quarter. For the year-to-date, total operating expenses were $33.4 billion for an efficiency ratio of 59.4%, improving 270 basis points from the prior year and in line with our target. Our year-to-date compensation ratio net of provisions was reduced to 30%. We remain committed to paying for performance and delivering operating leverage for shareholders. Quarterly non-compensation expenses were $6.2 billion, 30% higher year-over-year, driven largely by higher transaction-based expenses. Additionally, given the strong pull-through of incentive fees this quarter, we made a tax efficient charitable contribution of approximately $450 million as part of a planned acceleration of our philanthropic efforts. We also expect to make a meaningful contribution in the fourth quarter. Together, these actions will pull forward at least five years of planned charitable giving. The impact of our charitable contributions on quarterly EPS was approximately $1, while the impact on ROE and ROTE was approximately 1.1 percentage points each. Our effective tax rate for the year-to-date was 20.4%, and for the full year, we continue to expect an effective tax rate of approximately 20%. Now on to slide 11. Our common equity Tier One ratio was 12.4% at the end of the third quarter under the standardized approach, 100 basis points above our current capital requirement of 11.4%. Regarding recent regulatory developments, we welcome the Federal Reserve's rule finalization to enhance the transparency and accountability of the CCAR stress test and reduce the volatility of capital requirements. We also recognize the progress of the Basel III endgame and G-SIB surcharge proposals and are hopeful for finalization by the end of the year. Collectively, these developments represent meaningful progress towards a more balanced and risk-sensitive regulatory capital framework that preserves the strength and resilience of the banking system. As the rules are finalized, we support appropriately calibrated requirements that are aligned with the risks firms actually take and look forward to the timely completion of these reforms. We expect regulatory focus to soon shift towards liquidity regulation reform. We currently have over $570 billion in average global core liquid assets, representing approximately 25% of our total assets, and our liquidity coverage ratio is among the highest in our peer group. In the quarter, we repurchased $3 billion of our common stock and paid $1.5 billion in dividends. We continue to have significant capacity to deploy capital prudently in service of clients while maintaining an appropriate buffer. In conclusion, our third quarter performance reflects the strength of our client franchise, which has been bolstered by years of strategic execution. We've built market-leading franchises, deep relationships, and a higher and more durable revenue base. We remain focused on delivering strong returns while continuing to invest in our people, technology, and client franchises to drive long-term earnings growth and deliver for our shareholders. With that, we'll now open up the line for questions. Thank you. Please stand by as we assemble our queue. If you would like to ask a question during this time, simply press star then the number one on your telephone keypad. If you would like to withdraw your question, press star then two on your telephone keypad. If you're asking a question and are on a hands-free unit or a speakerphone, we would like to ask that you use your handset when asking your question. Please limit yourself to one question and one follow-up question. We'll take our first question from Glenn Schorr with Evercore ISI. Hi there. Thank you. First one on trading and markets. The results are nothing short of awesome. There's a short-term and long-term question I have. The short term is just simple. Is there anything unique in the quarter like related situational awareness or anything like that would contribute to the quarter such that we don't over model in the fourth quarter? The bigger picture question I want to ask you is, there's so many developments going on, tokenization, agentic trading, DeFi vaults, prediction markets. All these theoretically would nip at the core of your great markets business, but obviously you're not standing still. So maybe you could talk about where you're making investments and how you see some of those things, how we should think about that in conjunction with your markets platform. Thank you. Sure. Thanks, Glenn, and good morning. On the first point, I don't see anything that I would call out. Denis, do you? Yeah. Don't see anything I'd call out just on the first thing, just to put that aside. On your second question, obviously we've seen market structure evolve with technological advancements over long periods of time. We've talked about that for a long time, and as a leading market maker and risk intermediary, we have to continue to invest in technologies, infrastructure, capabilities to make sure we're supporting our clients at the cutting edge, and I think we continue to do that. I know you'll remember, Glenn, that it was not too long ago that people were concerned about electronification and equities trading and its impact on our business. But as we sit here today, the opportunity set for us is greater than what anyone could have contemplated when you look at our equity revenues and the way we adjusted and the way the business has evolved. Today, tokenization is obviously an important trend. We see it across asset classes. We were publicly supportive of CLARITY passing. It wasn't perfect, but we thought it would be good to give the market more clarity, no pun intended, and ensure investor protection. In the absence of that, we're already seeing agencies take steps to provide clearer rules for market, and we're very engaged in those dialogues. We continue to invest and closely monitor the developments, both for opportunities but also for risks. The developments are obviously creating more products, greater activity, potentially new clients, broader distribution channels. Naturally, when you look at these things, they expand the TAM for our business, and that's one of the things that's interesting and exciting. At the same point, we remain very focused on ensuring that we're well-positioned to serve our clients as these markets evolve. We've been investing in companies in the digital asset border market infrastructure space for years, and remain very focused on that. We've been building capabilities such as the GS DAP, where we were early in building our own rails for digital assets. We've tokenized bonds. We have a number of money market funds that are tokenized, real estate for certain clients, and so we've been focused on trying to be at the edge of some of those activities, although I'd say broadly, those activities are very small at this point. We're participating in a range of market developments. In July, we participated in the launch of DTCC's tokenization service, and we're now actively assessing scalable use cases that we could put within it. We expect over time, the underlying technology can drive greater efficiency, automation, streamline processes, reduce costs, take away friction, improve liquidity across asset classes. We are going to remain focused on this. I think you are right to raise it as something that requires attention, but I would say the activity so far is small and at the margin. We are going to continue to have real resources thinking about how these changes can evolve over time. I think it is one of the reasons when you think about, for example, electronification, we have managed to manage disruption or change in the equity business so well. We use that as a little bit of a guideline. I hope that is some helpful color. Yeah, you have not put any thought into it. No, I am kidding. Thank you. That was very helpful. I have covered you guys since, I guess the IPO. I have seen some transitions in management, and Goldman just gets stronger each step of the way. This one seems to be being managed pretty methodically. There were just some articles recently that talked about an acceleration. I do not know, David, if you want to address any of that just to keep the record straight. I appreciate it. Thanks. No, sure. I appreciate the question because some of the articles, the articles create noise. I will just start with, Glenn, I am super pleased with the progress the firm has made since we laid out our strategy at our Investor Day. The execution, this team has worked to really grow the firm significantly, and I think we have really made it increasingly durable. I have to say, at the point we are at now where we see the benefits of the effort that the broad team has made, I am really enjoying the job. More importantly, as a team, we are super excited about what is in front of us in the coming years and how we can continue to grow the franchise and really accelerate the earnings potential of the firm. I just want to be clear, there is no succession transition or timeline underway at Goldman Sachs. The Board and I are singularly focused on our strategy to grow the firm and continue to serve our clients with excellence. Thank you. We will take our next question from Erika Najarian with UBS. Thank you. Our conclusion is they're a highly idiosyncratic to non-correlated set of names, but we had a couple of different names that we ended up taking incremental impairments against in the quarter. We don't think it's necessarily the signal of something else to come. But it was appropriate for those individual names, and so we took the impairments and put it through in the third quarter. Very good. Then as a follow-up, you talked about it earlier in the year about the leaning into Asia and the success that you've had, and you touched on it again today, the Asian markets and the equity financing when the execution, you guys obviously benefit from. Are there any other opportunities globally where you can lean into new markets and get the benefits that you're seeing similar to what you did with Asia? I think there are opportunities all over the world where we can continue to lean in. What we found particularly attractive about Asia is that we felt that we were quite under scale, and the opportunity was available with clients on attractive economic and risk terms. And so it was the most attractive place geographically to drive incremental penetration and scale, and that's why we made it a priority. But there are plenty of other places around the world that we could continue to choose to drive incremental growth as well. Thank you. We'll take our next question from Chris McGratty with KBW. Oh, great. Thanks for squeezing me in. David, more of a high-level question. Your outperformance on your ROE to targets, maybe a comment or two on your views on how much is cyclical versus structural. I appreciate the question, Chris. I think a lot of it is we're structurally running the firm as a broader, more durable franchise with higher fundamental returns. I'm not going to speculate on through the cycle as to how the returns balanced out. But what I will say when I go back over the last five years, I remember sitting on this call for multiple years, including as recently as a couple of years ago, when we were very confident that we could get the firm running through our targets through the cycle, and there was a lot of skepticism about that. The reason the returns are significantly elevated is because we've significantly grown the breadth and the base of the firm. We've significantly changed the operational structure and the durability of the firm, and that's led to higher structural returns. There's a big strategic result of an investment over a long period of time. I will say, at the moment, and I've said it on the call three times, we're in a very good environment. We're in a top quartile environment. Does that flatter what will be the average returns through the cycle? Absolutely. But structurally, the base returns of the firm have been meaningfully uplifted over the last five years. Perfect. Then second follow-up would be the midterms. I think there's a divided view of whether a divided government is good for activity or perhaps a headwind. Where do you stand on if the futures markets are right about a divided government, how that could play into your capital markets business? Thanks. First of all, the election doesn't occur for another month, and in politics, a month is an eternity, so we'll see how the election plays out. I'm not a good pundit, nor are the prediction markets or the futures markets a good pundit of exactly what the environment will bring after the election as we head into 2027. So, we'll watch that and be prepared for whatever comes our way. Thank you. At this time, there are no additional questions. Ladies and gentlemen, this concludes The Goldman Sachs Group third quarter 2026 earnings conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect. title: Goldman CEO David Solomon Says Firm Is ‘Very Well Positioned’ Despite Global Uncertainties - GS Stock Gains On Q3 Earnings Beat - TradingView
content: Goldman Sachs (GS) on Tuesday reported better-than-expected third-quarter results, with strong growth in its equities business helping lift revenue and earnings above estimates. The bank reported revenue of $18.68 billion and diluted earnings per share (EPS) of $17.01, beating Fiscal AI estimates of $17.92 billion and $14.84, respectively. The stock was trading 3% higher at the time of writing. Solomon Highlights Client Relationships And Long-Term Growth David Solomon, chairman and CEO of Goldman Sachs, said clients continued to turn to the firm for its advice, execution and financing capabilities, despite a complicated operating environment. “Notwithstanding the current complexity and uncertainty in the world, we remain very well positioned to continue to deliver for our clients,” Solomon said. He added that Goldman’s market-leading franchises, deep relationships and continued investments would help drive long-term earnings growth. Solomon also added that it was the firm’s second-highest quarterly net revenue. It posted a record net revenue for the first nine months of the year. Equities revenue reached $6.44 billion, up 72% from a year earlier. Fixed income, currencies and commodities (FICC) revenue was $3.47 billion, essentially unchanged year over year. Global Banking & Markets revenue increased 32% to $13.46 billion. Investment banking fees rose 21% to $3.22 billion, while Asset & Wealth Management revenue grew 14% to $5.05 billion. Goldman Sachs said its investment banking fee backlog decreased from the end of Q2 and decreased slightly from the end of 2025. Goldman reported an annualized return on common equity of 18.7% for the quarter. Its efficiency ratio for the first nine months of 2026 was 59.4%, compared with 62.1% in the same period last year. Operating expenses rose 20% year over year to $11.31 billion, but declined 3% from Q2. The firm returned $4.49 billion to common shareholders during the quarter, including $3 billion in share repurchases and $1.49 billion in dividends. Goldman also declared a quarterly dividend of $5 per share, payable Dec. 30, 2026. Retail sentiment on Stocktwits climbed to ‘extremely bullish’ from ‘bullish’ a day earlier, while message volume remained ‘high’ over the past 24 hours. Chicago Federal Reserve President Austan Goolsbee said financial bubble unwinds can get ugly depending on leverage, when asked what a potential unwinding of the artificial intelligence (AI) trade might look like. Speaking on Semafor's Compound Interest podcast, Goolsbee described a conditional scenario in which the fundamentals are not there and the AI trade proves to be a bubble. He noted that the U.S. has experienced bubbles before, including in the recent past, whose unwinds “can get ugly” depending on the leverage associated with them. Goolsbee said an AI unwind could resemble the experience with internet infrastructure investment. He recalled infrastructure being built around expectations of 20% annual growth, only for the growth rate to come in at 7% annually, which he described as still pretty strong. However, builders massively overbuilt, leaving an overhang. Goolsbee said the internet-era overbuilding, where growth fell short of expectations, was “slightly different” from an “old-fashioned bubble.” Asked about Former Fed Chair Alan Greenspan's view that the Fed could not deflate bubbles in real time without causing wider economic pain, Goolsbee said economists have a very significant debate about whether the Fed should prevent bubbles, pop them or clean up afterward. The Fed president also expressed increasing nervousness that AI investment was becoming a source of old-fashioned overheating demand. He cited conversations with Illinois businesses reporting difficulty finding electricians, elevated construction costs and one-year waiting lists for electrical components amid competition with data centers. Goolsbee distinguished between increased data-center activity at the expense of other sectors and overheating across the broader economy. He said AI had not overheated aggregate demand, but was starting to. Conditions were starting to feel like aggregate overheating, with AI data-center cost increases spreading beyond directly related industries, he said, warning that further increases spreading into general services would be problematic. Goolsbee said rates could come down if there is evidence that inflation is heading back toward 2% while maintaining full employment. title: Lawmaker accuses GS Retail of inflating supply costs through unnecessary middlemen - 헤럴드경제
content: GS Retail has been accused of inflating product costs by routing purchases through unnecessary middlemen, hurting franchise owners' margins in the process. Democratic Party of Korea lawmaker Han Min-su raised the allegation Monday at a National Assembly audit of the Financial Services Commission. "Unnecessary vendor intermediaries in the supply chain are pushing up consumer prices and cutting into franchise owners' margins," Han said. "Is there effectively no oversight mechanism at all?" According to documents Han released, a vendor company called Hanbyeol began consulting with GS Retail on store listings in October 2020, before the firm was even incorporated. Hanbyeol was formally established as a corporation in January 2021 and registered as a GS Retail partner the following month. GS Retail sourced batteries through Hanbyeol at supply prices 120 percent higher than those of rival CU, which purchases batteries directly. From 2022 through recently, Hanbyeol recorded 17 billion won ($12.7 million) in sales to GS Retail. The company employs just three people and posted sales of 7.4 billion won last year. Han also said Hanbyeol carried no inventory assets whatsoever. Vendor companies are generally expected to purchase products in advance and deliver them to distribution centers, but Hanbyeol's financial statements showed no inventory at all. Han further raised allegations that GS Retail had entrusted supply contracts to a so-called "revolving-door" firm — one set up by a former GS Retail employee. "GS Retail laid the groundwork and let this company collect a toll while doing nothing," Han said. "When allegations surfaced of a connection to the owner family, GS Retail scrambled to downplay them." He added that GS Retail appeared to have handed Hanbyeol's chief a lucrative arrangement. GS Retail Executive Vice President Oh Jin-seok said the company is "closely examining what internal issues may exist."

title: The Cheap Adventure Bike That Makes A Used BMW GS Look Like A Financial Mistake - HotCars
content: Subscribe to the HotCars newsletter to never miss an update The BMW GS has evolved into something of an institution within the adventure community. Even though it is one of the most expensive ADVs on the used market, especially one with a few BMW-approved accessories, it is still incredibly popular. For most adventure enthusiasts, it has become the default choice, but we feel that there are a selection of more affordable options that all do a better job. Price is also only part of the problem. The GS weighs well over 500 pounds, and has a relatively tall seat height. It is easy to ride around this on the street, but it becomes far more challenging to deal with once you have your first spill off-road. Lifting one of these bikes is pretty easy on a flat surface, but very few trails offer that level of convenience. While these bigger adventure bikes are great tourers, they can sap one’s confidence off-road. For most riders, the whole point of owning an ADV is to go exploring off-road, and everything else is secondary. The solution comes in the form of a lighter middleweight, which offers a better balance between off-road competence and touring comfort. Today, we have a wide selection of impressive middleweights to choose from, with pretty much every major manufacturer producing one. It is fair to say that the Tenere 700 gave the middleweight market the shot in the arm it needed. Up until it made its global debut all the way back in 2019, most middleweight options were pretty heavy, relatively slow, and generally failed to capture the imagination. The Tenere, on the other hand, was light, fast, and promised us Dakar-level capability with the pre-production T7. Naturally, its final version was a little watered down, but not quite as much as people speculated. It was still a hard-edged off-road oriented machine. Customers in the US had to wait another two years, but it was worth the wait, and Yamaha actually struggled to keep up with demand for a time. Five years later, the competition has increased, and the price of the Tenere has gone up, yet it still offers sensational value to the right buyer. Most middleweight adventure bikes make use of reliable, modern twins, but out of all the 270 degree parallel-twins currently on the market, the CP2 is inarguably the most reliable. In fact, it is one of the most reliable motorcycle engines ever produced, at least when it comes to larger displacement bikes. When it comes to motorcycles that are used for travel, the kind of peace of mind is a genuine point of difference. Like most modern crossplane twins, it does a great job of emulating a V-twin. Even though 73 horsepower may not seem much when compared to its direct rivals, the way it delivers its power makes it a fun bike to ride out in the real world. Pretty much all of its torque is available from around 2,000 RPM, so the roll-on power is exceptional, and it doesn’t have all that much weight to lug around in the first place. The Tenere was initially a back-to-basics offering, and was intentionally sparsely equipped in an effort to keep the price down. While the rugged simplicity of the original was appealing to some, many adventure enthusiasts lamented its glaring lack of features when compared to its most direct rivals. Yamaha responded in kind by gradually updating the platform, and now, five years after it was first released in the US, it is very much the finished article. A ride-by-wire throttle was introduced, and this enables the two ride modes. It also gets ABS and traction control, which are both switchable. The original bike had a robust LCD dash, but the latest bike gets a big TFT dash with smartphone connectivity. In our opinion, these updates are all there simply to keep up with what the competition has on offer, but the most meaningful update came in the form of an improved rear shock. It was easily the biggest gripe with the original bike, and the fact that Yamaha listened to customer feedback says a lot about the brand. Unfortunately, every motorcycle is a compromise. With the extra effort Yamaha put into making the Tenere more competent off-road, you do lose some level of touring comfort. Out of all the middleweight bikes currently competing in this space, the Yamaha might actually have the worst seat. It is essentially a dirt-bike seat which works great while you are standing up off-road, but after around an hour on the highway, pretty much everything below your waist will lose feeling. For riders who will be using their ADV for long distance travel, this can be a deal-breaker, but there are aftermarket solutions available. The other factor counting against the Tenere is how much the competition has improved over the years. It lacks a certain level of sophistication, and certainly feels more like a budget offering than a late model GS would. But, if you want a more sophisticated version of the Tenere, Yamaha will gladly point you in the direction of the new World Raid edition which has a host of additional features, including an IMU-backed electronics suite, uprated KYB suspension, and a long-range fuel tank. Its tasteful Intensity White livery also gives the bike a premium feel. It is well worth considering, especially when you take into account the fact that its base price of $13k is still $3k less than what you would have to fork out for a five-year-old BMW. Objectively speaking, that is sensational value. But, the base model still has its place, and honestly makes that used GS look like a pretty poor financial decision when you look at the price difference. We want to hear from you. title: Granny G’s Celebrates MN’s Women Athletes With Hot Dogs Fried in Butter - Racket
content: At Minneapolis's North Star Deli, the menu and the decor are guided by a love of old-school Minnesota hockey. You’ve got your Herb Brooks Focaccia, your Gump’s Green Wrap, your Dino Italian Sub. Every surface is covered in memorabilia—Slap Shot figurines and Jesse Ventura action figures accompany vintage North Stars gear, a nod to the stuff chef Pedro Wolcott fell in love with, improbably, when he was introduced to Minnesota and hockey while watching The Mighty Ducks as a kid growing up in Panama. But one thing about old-time hockey? Not a lot of women in the mix. And Wolcott, looking around his Kingfield sandwich shop, thought it might be fun to do something with more of a femme focus. He has a daughter, after all—shouldn’t she see herself represented in sports and in her dad’s restaurant? “The women do so great, I don’t know why we never give them their due,” Wolcott says. (He’s right; nobody say anything about how the Lynx season ended.) This was the inspiration behind Granny G’s, Wolcott’s new hot dog trailer, where the dogs have names like The Lynx Glizzy (bacon bits, sauerkraut, caramelized onion) and Granny’s Kimchi Kick (gochujang spicy mayo, kimchi slaw, fried jalapeños, and wontons). Portraits of Olivia Miles by local artist Adam Johnson (of Naz Reid yard sign fame) greet you as you walk up to the truck, and the inside of the space, though tiny, is packed with more stuff: hockey sticks, pennants, grinning StudBudz. “This is like a typical food trailer in New Orleans,” Wolcott says, likening the decorations to those in over-the-top Big Easy spots like Turkey and the Wolf. “If I could have a TV in here with VHS playing, I would.” The focus is on Minnesota’s women’s sports teams, but New Orleans isn’t the only other city from which Wolcott draws inspiration. “These are upstate New York-style hot dogs, so we fry them in butter,” he says. He’s a longtime fan of Walter's Hot Dog Stand, which serves split-grilled dogs like these in its National Register of Historic Places-designated spot in Mamaroneck, New York. As for the chili? Wolcott has always loved the chili from Tommy’s in Los Angeles, where they slap the stuff on everything from burgers to breakfast burritos. But far-flung as Granny’s meaty muses may be, the ingredients are very local. Wolcott gets his hot dogs and sausages from Kramarczuk's in Northeast, and the “meats” for the vegan versions come from the Herbivorous Butcher. All of the buns are baked by Turtle Bread on Chicago Avenue. I don’t know that I’ve ever had a hot dog fried in butter before, but this method—dogs are butterflied, then fried—gives you a really snappy sausage, as rich and decadent as you’d expect a hot dog fried in butter to be. I’ve also never been to Tommy’s in L.A., but I love the chili that tops Granny’s Chili Cheese Dog ($9.99). Incredibly beefy and meaty, its richness is offset a bit by pickles, tomato, and sliced white onion, though I will caution you to grab a fistful of napkins if you order it, as this was one messy hot dog. Argentinian sausage is the buttery, splayed beef product that serves as the base of the Frost Power Play ($11.99), which is dressed with a wonderfully herbaceous chimichurri mayo and topped with crunchy potato strings. It’s a successful combination—perhaps more successful than the Frost power play was itself in the postseason this year. We’ll get the Walter Cup back in 2027, ladies. And lest your eyes pop at the price of a hot dog here (what are we, literally at a Frost game?), I’ll add that these churched-up little doggies are a whole-ass meal. I didn’t have my measuring tape handy, but I think they were about a foot long, and Granny G’s doesn’t skimp on the toppings. (Again: napkins!) Wolcott says he’s working to find a permanent spot in south Minneapolis for Granny G’s, but for now, he’s content periodically popping up at local businesses or just setting up in front of his Kingfield sandwich shop. Follow along on Instagram @grannyglizzys for info on upcoming pop-ups, including events later this month at Silverbird Coffee and Time Bomb Vintage. title: Korea Expressway Corporation Defeats GS Caltex 3-1 - 조선일보
content: Moma's 25 points lead team to first tournament victory in Yeosu Cup [Yeosu=Sports Chosun Na Yurim Reporter] Moma smiled. The Korea Expressway Corporation volleyball team defeated GS Caltex with a set score of 3-1 (25-18, 25-18, 20-25, 25-19) in a group stage match at the 2026 Yeosu·NH Nonghyup Cup Professional Volleyball Tournament held at Jinnam Gymnasium in Yeosu on the 12th. Korea Expressway Corporation, which secured their first victory in the tournament, was led to victory by Moma’s 25 points, Kang So-hwi’s 13 points, and Mami’s 10 points each. This match was the GS Caltex debut of Thai Asian quota player Thanacha. Thanacha, who played for Korea Expressway Corporation last season, signed with GS Caltex ahead of this season. Coincidentally, Thanacha’s first official match against her former team was also against Korea Expressway Corporation, with whom she had developed close relationships. Ahead of the match, acting head coach Kim Young-rae expressed mixed feelings, saying, “It felt strange. She was a player who often joked around, and (we grew close). It’s natural for players to want to experience different teams, and we respect that. Although we were disappointed, we believe the team has become more solid defensively with the addition of Mami.” GS Caltex head coach Lee Young-taek, who is also very familiar with the opponent, expressed optimism, saying, “I’m worried about how Thanacha will perform against Korea Expressway Corporation. However, she worked hard, and if she performs well in the early stages, I believe she can do well.” As expected, the match turned into a showdown between the two teams’ key aces: GS Caltex’s Silva and Korea Expressway Corporation’s Moma. GS Caltex took an early lead in the first set with Silva’s powerful spikes, but Korea Expressway Corporation countered with Moma’s serves. While GS Caltex struggled with unforced errors, Korea Expressway Corporation maintained a 50% attack success rate, scoring points whenever needed. Notably, Moma and Mami combined for 12 points in the first set, which proved decisive. Korea Expressway Corporation comfortably won the first set. The second set was closely contested, with the score seesawing back and forth. However, at 14-14, Korea Expressway Corporation pulled ahead by three points (17-14) with Moma’s back-row attack success, Kim Da-eun’s ace serve, and a blocking point by Moma against Thanacha’s attack after a long rally. GS Caltex turned to Silva to resolve the situation, but Moma blocked Silva’s attempts with blocking assists, leading to a fiery battle. Moma then exploded with points, contributing to the team’s 20th point. When Silva was blocked, GS Caltex began to falter. Korea Expressway Corporation capitalized on GS Caltex’s shaky reception and comfortably took the second set. GS Caltex took the third set. Thanacha, who had been quiet, began to shine. Although Kim Mi-yeon and Silva extended the lead with their points, Korea Expressway Corporation mounted a strong comeback with points from Kang So-hwi and Mami. In the middle of the third set, Park Jeong-ah, who was substituted in for the first time, changed the momentum with open attacks and blocks. However, GS Caltex, led by Silva, secured their first set win as Thanacha’s consecutive serving points in the closing stages proved decisive. The fourth set was also a close battle. GS Caltex led 10-6, but Korea Expressway Corporation capitalized on scoring opportunities to close the gap to one point. The intense battle continued, with GS Caltex pulling ahead and Korea Expressway Corporation chasing closely. Then, Mami’s serve achieved five consecutive points, allowing Korea Expressway Corporation to reverse the deficit instantly. Trailing 14-17, Korea Expressway Corporation scored six straight points to take a 20-17 lead. GS Caltex, drained of energy, completely collapsed, and Korea Expressway Corporation secured a decisive victory.
